what_matters.head: Wall Street rose after the Democratic sweep, led by Microsoft and Amazon, while chip and data-centre stocks fell.
what_matters.detail: The Dow rose 3%. Microsoft gained 6.7%, about 4.7 times its usual daily move, and Amazon 6.1%, about 3.3 times. Analysts quoted by CNBC said the result removed uncertainty, and that tighter rules favour the big cloud companies that already run AI data centres. The chip fund fell 3.1% and CoreWeave 9.9%. CNBC said Democrats who proposed data-centre moratoriums won the governor races in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, and voters sided against AI data centres in 40 of 41 local ballot measures.

what_matters.head: Seoul's chip sell-off deepened into the close: the Kospi ended 5.3% lower, with SK Hynix down 9.5% and Samsung 7.6%.
what_matters.detail: At 12:05 SGT SK Hynix was down 8.0% and Samsung 5.8%. The fall set off a sell-side trading curb during the day. Investing.com tied it to disappointing results from US chip designers Qualcomm and Arm overnight. Qualcomm fell almost 6% after hours: it expects $2.15–2.35 of adjusted earnings a share this quarter, against the $2.26 analysts expected. Arm dipped almost 2% despite beating analysts' figures (CNBC). Japan's Nikkei fell 1.7% and Singapore's STI rose 0.5%. None of this is in Wednesday's US prices.

what_matters.head: DBS's Q3 profit fell 5% from a year earlier to S$2.81B, below the S$2.96B Bloomberg's estimate expected, as trading income dropped 65%.
what_matters.detail: Net interest margin held at Q2's 1.87%, 9 basis points lower than a year earlier, and net interest income rose 4% to S$3.71B. Wealth assets reached a record S$544B, up 5% from Q2. The quarter's dividend is 81 cents: 66 cents ordinary plus a 15-cent capital return. The chief executive said the outlook has become more uncertain and gave no margin or income forecast. By 12:05 SGT DBS was down 0.3%, on volume 2.3 times usual for that time of day. OCBC reports tomorrow morning.

latest.tape_note: On Wednesday the S&P 500 fund rose 1.65%, about 2.6 times its usual daily move, and the Nasdaq 100 fund 1.0%. The chip fund fell 3.1% to a six-month low (Investing.com). VIX fell 20%. The 10-year yield fell 6 basis points to 4.89% and the dollar index 0.6%. US crude settled 8.3% lower at $88.12 a barrel. CNBC said traders bet a Democratic Congress will push Trump to end the Iran war; on 3 Nov Trump told the Financial Times he had no immediate plans to strike Iran. Gold rose 3.4% to $4,061 an ounce by Wednesday afternoon New York time as the dollar and yields fell (CNBC). The US dollar fell 0.2% against the Singapore dollar.

recent.headline: Wall Street rose after the Democratic sweep, led by Microsoft and Amazon, while chip and data-centre stocks fell.
The AP projects that Democrats win both the House and the Senate, and US stock futures and Asian chip stocks fell on it.
Marvell agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal, and Lumentum fell 18.6%, about 3.4 times its usual daily move.
Intel fell 28.6% on Friday, about 7.5 times its usual daily move, and the chip fund fell 8.2%, about 3.5 times usual.
Alphabet fell 12.3% on Thursday, about 8 times its usual daily move, on volume 3.6 times normal. It was the first full session after its Q3 results.
